statements.text: First-person methods are disciplined practices, found in phenomenology, psychotherapy and contemplative traditions, by which subjects train attention and emotional self-regulation to increase their sensitivity to their own experience. The phenomenological epoché, with its phases of suspension, redirection and receptivity, is the model.

sources.quote: are disciplined practices subjects can use to increase their sensitivity to their own experiences at various time-scales
The epoché has three intertwining phases that form a dynamic cycle
